stemMd: A city will replace broad-spectrum streetlights with narrow-spectrum lamps. Laboratory tests show that the new lamps attract fewer insects. Officials predict that bats feeding near streets will therefore obtain less food. Which finding most weakens that prediction?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The city has more lamps than a neighbouring town.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The laboratory found fewer insects around each new lamp.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Some residents prefer the colour of the old lamps.

options.label: D
options.textMd: In field trials, the insects attracted by the old lamps were mostly species that the local bats do not eat.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The new lamps use less electricity.

explanationMd: The prediction assumes that reduced insect attraction means reduced relevant prey. If the lost insects are mostly uneaten species, that link is weakened even though the laboratory result remains true.

distractorRationale.c: Resident preference is unrelated to prey availability.
distractorRationale.a: A cross-town count does not address the change in edible prey.
distractorRationale.b: This repeats the premise rather than weakening the inference.
distractorRationale.e: Energy use does not establish the bats’ food supply.
